intro.en: Quality inspection entails automatic or manual inspection lot creation, results recording, making usage decisions, and stock posting (if applica- ble). A dynamic modification rule enables a better and more practical quality control for logistics and the supply chain. Multiple specifications functionality brings many more choices to quality planning and quality inspection. Continuing with the quality planning master data that you set up in Chapter 2, this chapter delves into turning the same quality planning setup into a quality inspection. A quality inspection is a series of business process steps that users undertake to per- form inspection of a material, record any defects found, and make appropriate deci- sions to use the material in further logistics and supply chain functions. This chapter begins by walking you through the business processes in quality inspec- tion. Then it explores several optimization and productivity enhancement options available for quality inspection and quality planning. Next, the chapter covers material specifications, an intuitive and user-friendly functionality that caters to the specific needs of process industries. Then, we discuss the dynamic modification rule and how it helps in maintaining various inspection levels in the production or procurement pro- cesses. Next, we examine a case study that lets you configure a new inspection type, maintain its master data, and execute the business processes of quality inspection. Finally, this chapter covers the combined configuration basics of quality planning and quality inspection.

intro.en: Integrating with Materials Management Most of the QM features and functionalities that SAP S/4HANA delivers as standard offerings are sufficient for you to quickly and completely integrate QM with MM, and they don’t require much configuration. The key to successfully integrating quality management (QM) with materials manage- ment (MM) functionality depends on two elements: a well-planned setup of master data and exhaustive training of business process users. This chapter begins by conducting a quick check on configuration to ensure that the material type for which you need to activate QM is properly configured or is available. The next configuration object is the QM control key, which controls several business functions. Then, the focus of this chapter shifts toward maintaining the minimum QM master data required to run the relevant business processes. Because the master data creation processes are already covered in Chapter 2, in this chapter, you’ll find either the QM master data checklist or specific details within the master data you need to run the business processes. Finally, this chapter will also provide an understanding of end-to-end business pro- cesses involving various business scenarios in procurement and inventory manage- ment (IM) within the MM area. We’ll also cover a new functionality, first article inspection for the production part approval process, which can be used as an alterna- tive to status-based inspection. shows various inspection types that find greater usage in procurement and inventory management processes and into which you can integrate QM. We’ll cover all these inspection types and their applications in this chapter. intro.en: When a customer registers a product complaint, it’s far easier for the company to trace the origin of raw materials used in production when QM is an integral part of the production process. You have the option to integrate QM into several production processes as deemed applicable to the business requirements. Companies implementing QM are uniquely positioned to take advantage of various checks and balances on the quality of materials being produced. This ensures that there are no raw materials released to production until quality specifications have been adhered to and that no finished goods are dis- patched to the customer until they meet the quality standards set by the company. When defective goods are produced, quality issues not only affect the quality of the final goods produced but also result in loss of machine and man hours. Companies integrating QM in their production processes have access to a vast amount of data and information to help them make long-term decisions. This chapter begins by covering the configuration basics of setting up QM with produc- tion planning (PP). Then, the focus shifts to required QM master data and culminates in running the entire end-to-end business process of the production cycles. As you’ve seen the master data creation processes extensively in Chapter 2, here we provide the QM master data checklist only to ensure that it’s available in the system. Table 5.1 describes the various inspection types used in production processes that can also be used in QM. We’ll cover all these inspection types and their applications in this chapter. intro.en: QM integration with SAP S/4HANA Sales brings far greater visibility to the logistics, operations, and supply chain management processes. Integrating QM with SAP S/4HANA Sales helps organizations ensure that only accept- able and approved products eventually reach the customer. Organizations may also have requirements that the customer inspect the product before or after a product’s delivery. This chapter begins by covering the configuration basics of setting up QM with SAP S/4HANA Sales. Then, the focus shifts to required QM master data before culminating in running the entire end-to-end business process of various sales cycles. Because you’ve seen master data creation processes extensively in Chapter 2, here we provide the SAP S/4HANA Sales and QM master data checklist just for you to make sure that it’s available in the system. Table 6.1 consists of various inspection types that find greater usage in sales processes and into which you can integrate the QM area.

When integrating QM in the logistics and supply chain management processes, you need to take great care with test equipment that you use to conduct various quality tests. You can broaden the QM scope by inte- grating test equipment management into the business functions of plant maintenance. Building on the functions of plant maintenance (PM) and quality management (QM), SAP S/4HANA provides integrated test equipment management that combines important planning and processing functions of PM and QM. You should therefore view the combination of the planning and processing functions not as a separate area, but as an operating interface that combines the appropriate functions of the different areas for test equipment management and monitoring to facilitate business users meeting their business needs. It’s essential that all quality inspections and quality tests be undertaken using reliable test equipment and measuring devices that give accurate results. For this reason, test equipment management and its calibration are of paramount importance. Equipment or functional locations are defined as PM master data. A piece of equipment can be a boiler, a condenser, or a chiller, while a functional location can be a utility room or chiller room of a manufacturing plant. The steps to integrate QM with any of PM’s equipment or functional locations are the same that we show for test equipment man- agement in this chapter. Test equipment can be specific laboratory equipment such as a weighing scale that is used to conduct physical or chemical quality tests of materials. Note In this chapter, we’ll describe the functionality of PM in sufficient detail for the pur- poses of test equipment management; however, we can’t cover every possible busi- ness scenario. We’ll restrict the scope of this chapter to typical and routine business processes that use PM, QM, and materials management (MM). Due to the integrated nature of QM with other areas, it’s always best to coordinate with experts or consul- tants of other SAP areas to ensure meeting end-to-end business scenarios of a client where SAP S/4HANA is being implemented. The business process requires that you fulfill the requirements of managing the monitoring of test equipment according to relevant quality standards. To do this, the 7 Integrating with Plant Maintenance monitoring and test equipment (referred to as test equipment in the rest of this chap- ter) requires that you maintain detailed data on device type, usage site, inspection frequency, inspection method, and acceptance criteria, as well as measures to take in case of unsatisfactory results. In addition, the business requirement is to list, evalu- ate, and make available the inspection results for the test equipment. The SAP system can meet the standard requirements. Note Given its very high importance in ensuring business continuity, you’ll find test equip- ment management in SAP via menu path Logistics  Quality Management  Test Equip- ment Management. We’ll start this chapter with the factors that you need to consider to help you decide which SAP S/4HANA system areas you need to implement to map the business pro- cesses of PM. Next, we’ll cover the configuration basics of the serial number profile that you’ll need for equipment, and then delve into covering the important master data required to run the business processes. We’ll also cover the business processes of QM integration with PM and will also discuss some PM reports available in the system. Finally, we’ll also discuss an end-to-end setup to successfully create an inspection checklist, which is a new functionality available in SAP S/4HANA 2023.

intro.en: Integrating with Embedded Extended Warehouse Management Embedded extended warehouse management in SAP S/4HANA makes it far more efficient and effective for companies to perform quality func- tions in logistics and the supply chain that involve complex warehousing functions. Warehousing operations are closely linked with the sales, procurement, production, and distribution (inbound and outbound) processes in the supply chain, as well as with financial accounting. Good warehousing management should both support the smooth flow of materials to and from the warehouse and provide useful information to run the operations within the warehouse. Embedded extended warehouse management (EWM) in SAP S/4HANA has led to the following massive simplifications:  Direct access to master data and configuration objects  Elimination of the core interface (CIF) for transferring master data  Reduction of redundant transaction objects in embedded EWM and SAP S/4HANA Note The queued remote function call (qRFC) is still required to transfer transaction data from and to SAP S/4HANA and embedded EWM (see Figure 8.1). Engage an SAP Net- Weaver consultant to ensure the required qRFC setup is up and running. The chapter begins by explaining the minimal configuration required to integrate QM with embedded EWM, followed by discussing the relevant master data setup. Next, we provide an end-to end walkthrough of the integrated business processes. The chapter concludes with reporting, including the warehouse management monitor. Note In this chapter, we’ll describe the functionality of embedded EWM in sufficient detail for the purposes of its integration with QM; however, we won’t cover every possible business scenario. We’ll restrict the scope of this chapter to typical and routine busi- ness processes that use materials management (MM), QM, and the embedded EWM 8 Integrating with Embedded Extended Warehouse Management areas only. Due to the highly integrated nature of QM with other areas, it’s always best to coordinate with experts or consultants in these SAP areas to ensure you’re meeting the end-to-end business scenarios of a client where SAP S/4HANA (with embedded EWM) is being implemented. Figure 8.1 Embedded EWM in SAP S/4HANA The following sections begin with covering only the configuration elements in embed- ded EWM that have a direct bearing on the QM processes.

intro.en: Batch management is an important part of a company’s ability to procure, produce, store, and sell material. The batch defines a quantity of material by characteristics unique to that batch. Those characteristics determine how the material in that batch is used, sold, or moved. Certain materials can be defined in SAP S/4HANA as being batch-managed. A batch is a quantity of material that represents a homogeneous unit with unique specifications. The batch of material may refer to a quantity of chemical that is produced in one pro- cess or a quantity of bottles of water that were filled on a certain filling line from a spe- cific tank. There are many ways in which a batch can be defined. In SAP S/4HANA, the batch is used to identify units of material as they move through the system. The batch can have specific characteristics that enable it to be identified and used within the materials management (MM) or production planning (PP) functionality. This chapter describes the processes involved in creating and changing a batch and the process of batch determination. The first section gives an overview of the batch and how it’s used in industry. We’ll start out this chapter by covering the configuration settings needed to start using the batch management functionality in the SAP S/4HANA system. After configuration, we cover the requisite master data, followed by the business processes associated with batch management, such as manually creating a batch master and how the system automatically creates the batch master during various business transactions. We’ll then discuss specialized but important batch management topics, such as automatic batch determination, active ingredient management, batch derivation, and shelf-life expiration of batches. The chapter will conclude with some important batch manage- ment reports, including the Batch Information Cockpit.

intro.en: In process industries such as chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and food, com- panies that integrate sample management into their business processes reap the greater business benefits of comprehensive information, data visibility, and traceability by putting the necessary quality controls in place. Manufacturers in general and process manufacturers in particular often require exten- sive visibility and traceability of every important material procured, produced, or received through a stock transport order (interplant transfer). The system’s standard options are limited when there is a need to have separated yet categorized physical samples that the quality inspectors and other laboratory personnel can record results of and use to make usage decisions. Sample management provides a comprehensive and in-depth solution to physical samples of various sources (externally procured, pro- duced in house, customer or supplier complaints, etc.). With sample management, the system supports the following types of sample generation:  Automatic generation of physical samples during inspection lot creation  Manual generation of physical samples—if needed, with reference to an inspection lot or other reference objects  Manual and multiple generation of inspection lots for existing physical samples  Sample data records For each physical sample, the system creates a physical-sample record, which contains the following essential information:  Sample number  Sample type (from goods receipt, from procurement or production, from customer complaints, from stability study)  Physical sample category (primary sample, pooled sample, reserve sample)  Sample origin (material, batch, order) In this chapter, we’ll explain the necessary plant settings that need to be in place. Then you’ll learn how to set up a sample-drawing procedure, which is an important master data step in sample management, followed by the checklist for quality management (QM) master data that you need to ensure is already in place. Then, the chapter moves 10 Sample Management on to goods receipt from the procurement process and how the system automatically creates planned physical samples of various sample categories. Next, we move on to how sample management integrates with production processes, especially for in- process or during-production inspection. The chapter ends with the configuration basics of sample management.

intro.en: Leveraging quality certificate functionality in your company’s procure- ment and sales business processes can bring about significant optimiza- tion, efficiency, and control. Quality certificates bring greater visibility and control to the quality-related documen- tation involved in procurement and sales. Procurement process optimization occurs when you implement incoming quality certificates. By putting the necessary controls in place, you can prevent the release of procured raw materials into production or the release of defective procured spare parts into maintenance until the accompanying incoming quality certificate from the supplier is available in the system. If a customer complains about a defective product, incoming certificates provide complete traceabil- ity of a supplier’s compliance when supplying raw materials by displaying whether the details noted in the incoming quality certificate adhered to your organization’s specifi- cations. You can also quickly and comprehensively set up and use outgoing quality certificates for a more diverse range of stakeholders than only customers to whom the company sells its products. The critically focused area in outgoing quality certificates is again QM master data, if you intend to ensure complete and comprehensive visibility and avail- ability of information. This chapter is logically divided into two sections: incoming quality certificates and outgoing quality certificates. In each section, we’ll discuss the important configuration and master data highlights, as well as explain how to use the different certificates in your business processes.

intro.en: The goal of problem notification should be to form a business workflow across several specialist departments. The main task of the notification system is to handle external and internal complaints in connection with suppliers and customers, as well as trace problems in the production processes. The communication of quality-related complaints is one of the touchstones of every company’s customer-supplier relationship, whether it’s internal or external. Compa- nies examining the overall business context of complaints discover how a complaints process requires the involvement of multiple areas: materials management (MM), pro- duction planning (PP), SAP S/4HANA Sales, and, of course, QM. This results primarily in the need for a smooth notification processing workflow supported by suitable tools, such as automated notification systems. In this chapter, we’ll provide a comprehensive example that’s based on logistic core pro- cesses, and the same principles can be put to use without great difficulty in all commer- cial implementation areas, whether they are trade, production, or service areas. This example will highlight the business needs and technical requirements of quality notifi- cations. We’ll first provide an overview of how quality notification works within a work- flow in general and set up our example, then discuss how the different SAP S/4HANA areas use quality notification, and finally delve into the different tools you can use for specific tasks. Although this chapter will show a customer complaint that triggers qual- ity notification creation, companies can also leverage quality notifications for attending to nonconformance or initiating corrective and preventive actions, which is also dis- cussed in this chapter.

intro.en: Engineering change management and SAP S/4HANA change manage- ment tools find extensive application in several SAP logistics and prod- uct lifecycle management areas. These are essential tools to master because they offer far better and in-depth controls to changes in the master data than managing it through authorization controls. Engineering change management and associated change management tools in SAP S/4HANA offer extensive control in managing important master data in the QM area and can be easily set up to bring better visibility and accountability across the busi- ness processes. Engineering change management also has applications in other logis- tics areas of the SAP S/4HANA system and enables users to appreciate and take better advantage of the reporting features that are available. This chapter begins with the important configuration needed to set up and integrate engineering change management in QM, specifically for the task list (an inspection plan). Then, it covers how you can integrate SAP Business Workflow with engineering change management, with the engagement of an SAP Business Workflow consultant. We’ll show you how to set up a user status profile and how it controls the business functions. With the necessary configuration in place, we’ll move on to cover the change master. A change master doesn’t offer as strong, elaborate, or comprehensive options as newer SAP Fiori tools such as the change record, engineering record, and the man- agement of change process do. Briefly, the chapter covers the following four change management tools for master records:  Change master  Change record  Engineering record  Management of changes Now, let’s begin with the necessary configuration in engineering change management for the change master. 13 Engineering Change Management

intro.en: Audit management helps companies comprehensively attend to various external and internal audits and ensure legal, regulatory, and environ- mental compliance. An audit is a systematic examination that a company undertakes to determine to what extent an object meets previously specified criteria. Audits are usually performed using question lists that represent the criteria. Audit management is an effective cross- application component that can support different audit types, such as supplier audits, customer audits, internal audits, and environmental audits, as well as other kinds of assessments, examinations, inspections, or revisions. It helps companies comply with legal requirements or industry standards. It supports all phases of auditing, from the planning of a comprehensive audit program and the individual audits to the definition of the audit criteria or question lists to the actual auditing process and assessment of the audit object in the audit report. Audit management also supports defining and monitoring corrective and preventive actions based on audit findings. It’s an effective tool for the evaluation of all audit-related data. This chapter begins with setting up the required master data you need to put in place for audit management. Then, it covers the business processes of audit management, audit monitoring and evaluation, and available productivity enhancement tools. We then evaluate the possibility of using the specific inspection type available in the QM area to manage supplier audits. Finally, we cover the configuration basics of audit man- agement.

Manufacturers often conduct stability studies, which test materials in a variety of conditions over a period of time to determine how the materi- als react/change under different storage conditions. In quality manage- ment, stability studies with (and without) material functionality can assist in the material testing and validation process. A stability study assesses and evaluates the physical and chemical conditions of a phys- ical sample in various storage conditions. Industries in general, and process industries in particular, routinely conduct stability studies on raw material from suppliers to ascertain whether the shelf life and other physical and chemical parameters meet the company’s needs. Companies also conduct stability studies on their own produced goods to evaluate changes in the product’s physical or chemical properties over an extended period of time. Another area in which you’ll find extensive use of stability studies is during a new prod- uct’s development. For a stability study, it’s important to create an initial sample, which then undergoes results recording and a usage decision to confirm whether the initial sample must proceed with a complete set of activities related to the stability study. This chapter covers a more diverse and in-depth option of conducting a stability study with a material; the other option is without a material, which offers fewer options and flexibility. The chapter begins with discussing the integration workflow associated with a stability study. This is then followed by covering the details of the important QM master data that you need to initialize the stability study with a material. We’ll then cover every option available in the long list of tasks available in the Action Box in the stability study. As needed, the chapter addresses cross-modular integration or attends concepts to aid in comprehension. Our example in this chapter is a hypothetical stabil- ity study of a still-under-development material with a special or secret project code of 800000004.

intro.en: Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan Companies are always looking for new ways to prevent or eliminate failures in the manufacturing of products or in streaming existing business processes. Failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) can help with preventing production and process failures. Failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) is a tool companies can leverage to ensure that they can attend to all product and process defects to bring about continuous busi- ness process improvements and minimize or eliminate product defects. FMEA has been an integral part of businesses in general and manufacturing industries in particu- lar for a significant time now. In fact, there are various industry standards that attend to FMEA in great detail. In this chapter, we’ll adopt a step-by-step approach to create FMEA and its items. These items are as follows:  Characteristic The specific production or process attribute that the company wants to monitor for possible failure.  Cause The factors that can cause a failure of the characteristic.  Effect How the failure impacts the production or business process.  Detection action What detection mechanism is in place to detect failure.  Preventive action What preventive action can prevent failure of the product or business process.  Severity The severity of failure for the production or business process. The chapter then moves on to cover the FMEA business processes, including calculat- ing the risk priority number (RPN). Then, the chapter covers the question list that you need as a checklist in your FMEA initiative. This will then be followed by discussing FMEA monitor and risk analysis. The chapter will also cover how to create and then integrate a control plan with FMEA. While we provide configuration tips and points 16 Failure Mode and Effects Analysis and Control Plan where applicable, the end of this chapter covers more of the important configuration basics in FMEA. Note If you want to get FMEA printouts according to the industry standards’ layouts/forms, such as QS9000 or VDA 96, then you’ll need to engage your SAP NetWeaver consultant to install Adobe Document Services (ADS) in your SAP S/4HANA system.

intro.en: Early Warning System informs you whenever any deviation or exception to an important business process occurs, allowing you to take timely action and thus minimize business disruptions. Early Warning System (EWS) is built on the same SAP S/4HANA system logistics infor- mation structures as other standard analysis tools and reports, with added flexibility that allows you to monitor and receive alerts for only the specific exceptions that are important to your business processes. For example, say that a critical raw material required for a production process is rejected during quality inspection. If so, then the system should immediately be able to alert procurement and production planners through EWS. It provides real-time updates and can be tailored to individual needs without the involvement of any custom ABAP development. EWS is delivered as part of the logistics area and can create alerts for individual busi- ness process owners in all the logistics functions, such as quality management (QM), shop floor control, purchasing, and plant maintenance (PM). In this chapter, we’ll explain how EWS can help you, and then we’ll provide the steps you need to get it up and running in your system.

Timely, accurate, and comprehensive information helps companies make better and faster business decisions. You can immediately start to use the many information systems, standard reports, standard analyses, and SAP Fiori apps available in SAP S/4HANA for QM and other logistics areas. This chapter provides detailed guidance on how to leverage several standard reports and SAP Fiori apps that are available in all areas of SAP S/4HANA. We’ll cover standard reports such as information systems that are available for day-to-day reporting, as well as many standard analyses and several SAP Fiori apps available to help business pro- cess owners make important and better decisions. After you become familiar with the features and functions for reporting, including tools and menu bars, it becomes easier to navigate to unexplored areas of reporting. In this chapter, we’ll cover the information systems of QM, including the options to lever- age several functions beneficial to business users, such as the ability to create various graphs from the data. After we cover the options for reporting with real-time informa- tion in the information systems, we’ll discuss how to report on historical data with stan- dard analyses available for the QM area, as well as some of the associated features, such as time series and ABC analysis. We’ll also cover the QM cockpit for evaluations, as well as the several SAP Fiori apps for QM in areas of analytics, master data, and transactions. Note For more reports and reporting options, we suggest that you read Chapter 12 on quality notification and Chapter 19 on quality control.

intro.en: Whether for procurement, production, or sales, it’s in a company’s larger business interest to maintain and improve quality controls across the entire logistics and supply chain operations. Quality control involves inspections at all stages, continuous monitoring, and inter- vening quickly to deal with unexpected events. You can leverage quality control tools to improve and optimize your business processes. In accordance with ISO 9000, qual- ity control entails working with techniques and activities that seek to monitor pro- cesses and remove the causes of unsatisfactory results. To remove these causes, companies need to undertake corrective and quality-promoting measures that prevent a defects recurrence. The focus of this chapter will be on supplier evaluation, quality level, and statistical process control. This chapter begins with the configuration basics that must be in place to start using supplier evaluation. Then, it covers the master data that needs to be set up for supplier evaluation, followed by the business processes and several additional functions that are available. Next, it covers the quality level and how the system keeps updating infor- mation over time (and with more data input from business processes). The quality level works when the dynamic modification rule is in place. The last section delves into cov- ering statistical process control, control charts, and various other quality control tools that are available. To maintain continuity among various sections of this chapter, the transaction and business data that we use in supplier evaluation business processes eventually leads to evaluating statistical process control (through control charts).

intro.en: The successful implementation of a Document Management System (DMS) project entails understanding the business needs and the business processes of a company. The next step is to map these business processes with relevant DMS features and functionalities. Finally, it’s also about ensuring that the necessary DMS configuration is in place for smoothly running the business processes. During an implementation of Document Management System (DMS) in SAP S/4HANA, when it’s established that certain types of hard-copy or soft-copy documents and digi- tal assets are going to be stored in DMS, the next logical step is to have intensive discus- sions and several workshops to agree on the DMS configuration objects. Configuration in DMS forms the basis on which the businfess processes of the company will run. For example, which functionalities of SAP S/4HANA will be integrated with DMS? How will the linking between SAP S/4HANA areas with DMS take place? What is the lifecycle of a document info record, and how can you maintain the structure, logical, and end-to-end links of a document info record during its entire lifecycle? DMS configuration is the first step that needs to happen in the SAP S/4HANA system. The configuration is the backend activity in the system, which is a foundation on which the business processes of DMS will run. Because it’s a backend activity and normally happens only once during the DMS implementation project, a lot of thought, deliberation, effort, time, and con- sideration must be accorded at the start of the DMS implementation project. This chapter offers a deep-dive into the DMS configuration and gives step-by-step instructions for setting up DMS in SAP S/4HANA. It highlights the guidelines and les- sons learned from actual DMS implementation projects that a DMS expert needs to consider when configuring and implementing DMS in an organization. The chapter begins with discussing the number ranges that must be configured so that they can be assigned to the document types later on. Creating document types and then assigning the previously configured number ranges is covered next. A docu- ment type, which holds a lot of information, controls, checks, and balances, is dis- cussed in detail. A document type also holds the key document lifecycle controls through statuses and the associated status network. The chapter then moves on to dis- cuss the master data and the associated business processes of DMS, followed by dis- cussing how to use the DMS search and reporting functionality. The chapter then focuses on the associated SAP Fiori app, Manage Documents, available to create and 20 Document Management System manage documents in DMS. The chapter concludes by showing how DMS integrates in the QM business processes, such as in results recording, usage decision, and even batch management. Note For more on DMS, see Document Management with SAP S/4HANA (SAP PRESS, 2020). We’ll start with the basic configuration settings needed to set up DMS.
